summary: Human skin, type II on the Fitzpatrick scale, with a synthetic skin map: the base with every layer: freckles, veins and marks.
_comment: A SYNTHETIC test skin (the lead's spike, 2026-10-26; OMF research 261026_R_SyntheticSkinAndEyeSets): Skin_FitzpatrickII's substance with a procedural map, the base with every layer: freckles, veins and marks. The map's colour comes from melanin and blood amounts per texel through a tabulated two-chromophore skin model, placed on the body in 3D (sun-exposed parts darker, palms and soles lighter, cheeks, nose, ears, fingertips and knuckles redder), so each tone gets its own regional colour; its average is held to the tone by the library's own calibration (tools/converters/fit/gen_synth_skin.py). No photograph, no AI. A draft to be judged in Studio beside Skin_FitzpatrickII_Clean_Base; the Detail token names the layer set. The lips and nails pair with the tone's own articles.
name: Skin_FitzpatrickII_Clean_SynthAll_s001_v01

sources.note: the synthetic skin map (layers: freckles, veins, marks): CC0 parts only (hm08, MPFB2's region masks and thickness map), a tabulated two-chromophore skin model (melanin 0.0119, blood 0.02 at the tone), seeded procedural noise and point processes; its average over the skin held to the Physically Based tone below; base_color_const is that tone x the map's peak factor
roughness 0.5 is the MEAN of the Skin_Pores roughness map

sources.why: subsurface_weight 1.0 and subsurface_color = the albedo: skin scatters throughout, and OpenPBR's default subsurface colour (light grey) would desaturate the tone. Phase21 (RD-P21-1, RD-P21-4): the scatter colour now FOLLOWS the base (subsurface_color connected to base_color_out), so it takes the map and the tint; before, it was pinned to the albedo and the tint was inert on skin in every tool (F-P21-3).

Phase07 7.3. Coat 0.1 at roughness 0.3 is MPFB2's 'enhanced skin' clearcoat (skin oil; CC0 shader settings, research Pass 3); coat_ior 1.5 is the value MPFB2 inherits from Blender (sebum is ~1.47). subsurface_scatter_anisotropy 0.8: tissue scatters strongly forward (a Henyey-Greenstein g of ~0.8 for skin). Fuzz 0.1 in the skin's own albedo, roughness 0.5: fine vellus hair seen at grazing angles, taking roughly the skin's hue (a light grey would put a grey rim on the darker tones); MPFB2 carries no fuzz, so the weight is kept low. Storm ignores the anisotropy (Learnings Storm S8), which adds ~1.2 to the rig's ΔE; Blender is the one honouring it.
